General.Description:
When former Special Forces operative Cole Regan is hired to retrieve a stolen bioweapons cache from the heart of a crumbling Eastern European city, he expects a routine extraction. What he gets instead is a week-long siege against a ruthless paramilitary organisation with nothing but his wits, his fists, and a dwindling supply of ammunition.

Iron Fist is a relentless, bone-crunching thriller set across rain-soaked rooftops, underground fight clubs, and abandoned industrial facilities. Marcus Webb pulls no punches — literally or figuratively — in this high-octane debut that moves at breakneck speed from the first chapter to the final explosive confrontation.

Cole Regan is not a hero in the traditional sense. He is calculating, morally ambiguous, and utterly ruthless when the situation demands it. Yet beneath the hard exterior lies a man haunted by past missions and the collateral damage that followed. When innocent lives hang in the balance, Regan must decide just how far he is willing to go — and whether he will recognise the man staring back at him in the mirror when it is all over.

A must-read for fans of Lee Child and Vince Flynn.
